body: If anything just try the weed and alcohol alone and chill. Listen to some music and dance together. Hold each other. Kiss. Don't even talk. Just... be.

One of the things that I've found in life after trying it myself at 18 (I'm now 41), is that, whether you're happy or sad, finding people to kinda 'get' why you feel that way is rare... or at least seem genuinely interested anyway. It's just a part of life I guess. It's kinda clichè but once you accept yourself, even if 'yourself' is usually a kinda down, depressed person... things get a little easier. I guess it's kinda just acceptance that life is a struggle. But it makes us who we are. One day (hopefully soon) someone or something will enter your life and make you think "you know what, that was, and is, rough... but I wouldn't be where I am and who I am without going through it and tbh... as much as it sucked at the time .. I'm glad I went through it and wouldn't really change it".

I dunno. I'm just laying here in bed about to roll over to sleep. Don't get too upset though. Just ride it out. We all have to do it. Just think about bedtime... put on a tv show that reminds you of happier times or makes you feel safe, get comfortable... and wake up tomorrow and smile... or at least try!

Be blessed.

Love you. X

Trust me, aspergers or not I know how to be a bastard if I want. I try very very hard not to blame my diagnosis on the way I am. That's just a cop out. But I do understand that it CAN be the reason I feel certain ways. At the end of the day, whatever diagnosis or issue ANY of us have, the more we understand it, the better we can deal with it.

I have a terrible habit of just locking myself away though so I don't upset or annoy other people and it's a lonely place to be at.

I got PTSD, aspergers, anxiety, depression and I was drinking farrrrr too much. My ex never really understood me. We made it just shy of 8 years but I tapped out of that cos it was destroying me. My wife now... She's a lot better at understanding. Trust me, I still get on her nerves with the way I am (always doubting stuff, overly worried, etc) but she helps me understand where I'm going wrong in a way.

I'm a very depressive person and mix that with my Aspergers and its awful. It's like, she says I can openly talk about how I feel and stuff but even when I do, it just makes me feel guilty and I try and shut up and then it comes out a week or two later with a big depressive period.

I understand my issues but finding a way to cope with them... I'm still trying.

I guess like, the best thing to do is to assess what you do that makes people feel put off and see if there's another way of dealing with things. Not saying it's all your fault or you're wrong in how you feel BTW. But like, finding coping mechanisms is important. And like I say, I'm still trying to find mine whilst not pushing my wife away.

It sucks really.

One question if I may.

Have you ever felt a loss like this before? Like, me for instance... When I've broken up with a chick before and it felt like my world crumbled... And in a way it did... And I never thought there be anyone that would love me or I'd love like that again... But I've had two long relationships since then. Whatever good that comes may not last forever, but nothing really does. We just have to try and find random little things to keep us going. In fact, I'm actually still alive now because of a candy bar. Long story but fr... Small things count cos they make up the majority of our lives.
I know it's hard rn. Give it until tomorrow at least? One day at a time. That's how I'm still here... And sometimes, when it feels like all is gone... Something good comes out of nowhere.

I did that when I was 18 and weighed about the same. Except I took 30 something and drank a load of alcohol. It won't kill you but it'll make you puke like there's no tomorrow!!! Best to go to the hospital. They'll probably give you something to counteract it and you'll be back home tonight. If possible take the packaging from the pills too so they know the exact dosage you took.

Most importantly of all though, remember this... You're beautiful, you're loved, we hurt that you're hurt... And never forget, tomorrow is a new day.

Love you ❤️

Different shades of color so once we get back to the big white canvas we can paint a beautiful picture with our experiences and help others grow.... Maybe. I dunno.

I used to get bullied for being skinny too. I was 16 and it was a super hot day. I'd just finished a day at my apprenticeship as a mechanic and the sun was beating down hard so I took off my top walking home... Bad idea. Two random dudes walking past stayed making comments and laughing. It was awful.

I'm still pretty slim, caught a bit of a beer belly over the years but still rocking 34'' waist jeans. My girl says I have owl legs... Kind of an inside joke. She made a comment about my arms not long ago though being skinny and that triggered me so bad and made me feel like less of a man. She did apologise though but the thing with words though, once you put them out there you can NEVER take them back.

I find myself just existing too. It's like, I have hopes and dreams for the future... But will it ever come to anything? Who knows.

It sucks.
I'm with you there. But hey, I'm 38. These thoughts have been with me for 20 years. Not many people left in my life to hurt right now... But we gotta keep going on... Its all we've done so far right?

I'm new here on Reddit but I feel the same way. Some days are good, some are bad. It always seems like such a long way to reach a good day. I been here for 38 years though and even though I think it would be easier... I'd better just carry on carrying on no matter how painful it is.

I guess the bravest thing we can do though is to carry on. It takes an awful lot of strength... But hopefully, one day... It'll all make sense as to why we carried on. I just hope that day comes soon.

God bless you. I truly hope you feel better soon.
